# Results — Study 612 (EM Debt Carry)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **emerging-
market sovereign bonds pay a fat spread over Treasuries: carry you actually collect** — rebuilt
on the index funds that package it: **EMB** (hard-currency EM sovereigns, EMBI Global Core,
listed 2007-12 so the GFC is on the tape) against the duration-matched **IEF** (7-10y
Treasuries), with the **EMLC** local-currency contrast from 2010-08. Both legs run twice —
total-return and price-only — so their monthly difference isolates the **coupon stream** (the
promised carry) from the price leg. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `1bff8a946cdf`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes, twice: **auto-adjusted (total-return)** and **price-only** — EMB, EMLC, IEF, SPY, BIL (public, no key) |
| Headline window | 2008-01-31 → 2026-06-30 (**222** complete months, **18.5** years — the common EMB+BIL window, GFC included) |
| EMLC contrast window | 2010-08-31 → 2026-06-30 (**191** months) |
| Benchmark | **IEF** — EMB's effective duration (~7y) sits on IEF's 7-8y, so the TR spread isolates the EM credit/carry premium, not a duration bet |
| Execution / costs | passive buy-and-hold decomposition; entry at the first month-end close of the common window (one documented, trivial lag — no timing signal to lag); ETF expense ratios (EMB 0.39%/yr, EMLC 0.30%/yr) already inside the tape; two one-way trades over 18.5y ≈ 0.5 bps/yr amortised |
| Inference | Newey-West HAC *t* (6 lags) on every serially-correlated monthly mean; Welch *t* on the risk-off group split; Sharpe races excess-vs-excess over BIL |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** EMB and EMLC are index **funds** — their tapes
> already contain every default, restructuring and ejection that happened inside the index
> (Venezuela 2017, Lebanon 2020, Russia + Ukraine 2022 …). The fund tape is **not**
> survivor-biased; what it *is* shaped by is the index rulebook (issue-size floors, liquidity
> screens), which we state rather than hide.

## The promised carry — the coupon pickup is enormous and mechanically real

Coupon component = total-return minus price-only return per fund; the pickup is EMB's coupon
stream minus IEF's.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| EMB coupon stream | **+4.97%/yr** (HAC *t* = **+35.2**) |
| IEF coupon stream | +2.46%/yr |
| **yield pickup (EMB − IEF)** | **+20.24 bps/mo = +2.46%/yr** · HAC *t* = **+20.09** (n = 222) |
| rolling-12m pickup | min **+1.30%** · median **+2.48%** · max **+3.42%** — positive in every 12-month window |

The *promise* is real, fat and never absent: EM sovereigns paid ~2.5%/yr more coupon than
Treasuries in every rolling year of the sample.

## The collected carry — the total-return spread does NOT clear the bar

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **TR spread (EMB − IEF)** | **+17.83 bps/mo = +2.16%/yr** · **HAC *t* = +0.99** (n = 222) |
| skew of the monthly spread | **−1.72** |
| $100 grows to | **$232.8** (EMB TR) vs **$170.2** (IEF TR) |
| EMB / IEF / SPY (CAGR, vol, excess Sharpe, maxDD) | +4.67%/yr · 11.44% · **0.35** · −26.7% — vs IEF +2.92%/yr · 6.71% · 0.27 · −23.2% — vs SPY +11.24%/yr · 15.72% · 0.68 · −46.3% |

Eighteen and a half years and $63 of extra wealth per $100 — and the spread *still* cannot be
statistically distinguished from zero (**t = 0.99**), because the crash months are that
violent. The +2.46%/yr promised pickup shrank to +2.16%/yr collected — and all of the
statistical evidence for it died in five windows (below).

## The carry-crash profile — it is insurance selling

Spread conditional on the equity tape, worst-decile SPY months vs the rest:

| leg | spread |
|---|--:|
| worst 10% SPY months (n = 23, cut −5.3%) | **−438.0 bps/mo** |
| all other months (n = 199) | **+70.5 bps/mo** |
| **risk-off gap** | **−508.5 bps/mo** · Welch *t* = **−4.84** |
| corr(spread, SPY) | **+0.69** |

And after stripping duration **and** the hidden equity beta (EMB excess on IEF + SPY excess,
NW-HAC 6 lags): **alpha = −19.35 bps/mo (−2.30%/yr), HAC *t* = −1.44**, with **b_SPY = +0.46
(t = +7.85)**, b_IEF = +0.77 (t = +4.71), R² = 0.57. More than half of EMB's variance is
duration plus equity beta, the "spread" loads on stocks at t ≈ 8, and the residual carry
premium is *negative* (insignificantly). A DIY IEF+SPY mix replicated the package with nothing
left over.

## The local-currency contrast — the FX leg eats the whole thing

Common EMLC window (2010-08 → 2026-06, n = 191):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| EMLC coupon stream | **+5.60%/yr** (pickup vs IEF +3.29%/yr, HAC *t* = +21.55) |
| **EMLC − IEF TR spread** | **−5.16 bps/mo = −0.62%/yr** · HAC *t* = **−0.24** · $100 → **$118.2** vs **$139.8** |
| EMB − IEF TR spread (same window) | +17.93 bps/mo = +2.17%/yr · HAC *t* = +1.24 |
| EMB − EMLC TR spread | **+23.09 bps/mo = +2.81%/yr** · HAC *t* = +1.81 |

The local-currency version pays an even fatter coupon (+5.6%/yr) and still **lost to
Treasuries** over 15.9 years — EM currency depreciation ate the entire pickup and more. The
hard-currency premium, such as it is, is a *dollar-denominated* phenomenon; the FX leg's bill
is ~2.8%/yr (the currency side of this trade is
[364-fx-carry-trade](../../364-fx-carry-trade/)).

## Third axis — does the spread survive the crises it insures?

Five fixed, documented risk-off windows; cumulative monthly TR spread (EMB − IEF) inside each:

| window | cumulative spread | months |
|---|--:|--:|
| GFC 2008 (2008-09 → 2009-03) | **−17.33%** | 7 |
| Taper tantrum 2013 (2013-05 → 2013-09) | −2.91% | 5 |
| EM stress 2018 (2018-04 → 2018-11) | −5.29% | 8 |
| COVID 2020 (2020-02 → 2020-04) | **−18.79%** | 3 |
| Rate/Russia 2022 (2022-01 → 2022-10) | −9.83% | 10 |

| ledger | value |
|---|--:|
| CRISIS months (n = 33) | **−164.1 bps/mo**, cumulative **−54.1%** |
| CALM months (n = 189) | **+49.6 bps/mo** (HAC *t* = **+3.38**), cumulative **+93.7%** |
| crisis-vs-calm gap | Welch *t* = **−2.15** |
| whole-sample cumulative spread | **+39.6%** |

All five windows are negative. The 33 crisis months hand back **58%** of everything the 189
calm months collected, and drag the whole-sample HAC *t* from **+3.38** (calm only) to
**+0.99** (all-in). **Arithmetically the spread survives (+39.6% cumulative); statistically it
does not** — the crises are exactly the events the spread was pricing, and they take the
evidence with them. Crisis drawdowns coincide with equities every time (daily peak-to-trough:
EMB −34.1% GFC, −26.5% COVID, −26.0% 2022 vs IEF −6.0%, −4.7%, −17.4%).

## Robustness

| variant | spread | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| NW lags = 3 / 6 / 12 | +17.83 bps/mo | +0.96 / **+0.99** / +1.10 |
| ex-GFC (2010-01+, n = 198) | +16.46 bps/mo | +1.17 |
| last decade (2016-07+, n = 120) | +23.46 bps/mo | +1.23 |

No lag choice and no subperiod pushes the collected spread anywhere near *t* = 2. The
coupon-pickup *t* (≈ 20-35) and the collected-spread *t* (≈ 1) are two different animals on
the same tape.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic monthly world with a planted TR spread, a planted coupon (25 bps/mo pickup) and
a planted risk-off beta:

| planted | spread (HAC *t*) | pickup (t) | risk-off gap (Welch *t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| spread = 0, β_SPY = 0 (null) | +4.54 bps/mo (**+0.61**) | +23.72 bps/mo (+42.4) | +26.1 bps/mo (**+1.21**) |
| spread = +30 bps/mo, β_SPY = 0.45 | +62.91 bps/mo (**+3.85**) | +23.72 bps/mo (+42.4) | −376.4 bps/mo (**−14.41**) |

Under the null neither the spread test nor the risk-off split manufactures significance;
planted values light up. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited to support the
real-tape stamps.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** (*Real on the coupon · None on the collected spread*). The **promised**
  pickup is mechanically real and fat: **+2.46%/yr at HAC *t* = +20.1**, positive in every
  rolling year. The **collected** total-return spread — the thing the claim actually asserts —
  is **+2.16%/yr at HAC *t* = +0.99** over 18.5 years (skew −1.72), and no lag choice or
  subperiod rescues it. Survivorship is not the issue (index funds carry their defaults); the
  crash months are.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The packaged carry is **hidden equity beta plus duration**:
  b_SPY = +0.46 (*t* = +7.85), R² = 0.57, and the NW-HAC alpha vs a DIY IEF+SPY mix is
  **negative** (−2.30%/yr, *t* = −1.44). The spread pays +70 bps/mo in calm months and hands
  back −438 bps/mo exactly in the worst equity decile (Welch *t* = −4.84) — insurance selling
  correlated at +0.69 with the stock market you already own. The local-currency version
  (EMLC) *lost* to Treasuries outright (−0.62%/yr, $118 vs $140). Access and costs are fine;
  what you can actually collect is beta you didn't need plus a left tail.
- **"Does the spread survive the crises it insures?" — MIXED.** Arithmetically yes:
  **+39.6%** cumulative spread survives all five windows. Statistically no: every window is
  negative, the 33 crisis months hand back **58%** of the calm-month carry (**−164 bps/mo**
  vs +49.6, Welch *t* = −2.15) and collapse the whole-sample *t* from **+3.38** to **+0.99**.
  The spread is compensation for exactly the events that keep eating it.
